subject.title: Telegram voice message delayed ~15 minutes before agent dispatch, then run aborts

question: What should OpenClaw guarantee when a Telegram voice update is old by the time it reaches dispatch and the resulting direct-message turn aborts before any final reply?
rationale: Source inspection shows no source message-date-to-dispatch guard and fallback behavior is conditional; choosing thresholds, restart behavior, and user-visible failure copy is a product/reliability decision before automation can safely repair it.

options.title: Define a narrow latency and abort fallback contract
options.body: Choose the source-age threshold, recovery action, and direct-message failure copy, then allow a focused Telegram repair with live proof.

options.title: Require live reproduction first
options.body: Keep the item blocked on a live Telegram repro before deciding whether the root cause is polling, spool, dispatch, or run-abort handling.

options.title: Split the no-reply recovery symptom
options.body: Leave this issue focused on pre-dispatch latency and route generated transcript-recovery delivery loss through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/91652.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow latency and abort fallback contract
recommendation.body: Choose the source-age threshold, recovery action, and direct-message failure copy, then allow a focused Telegram repair with live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the most recent history on the current Telegram ingress spool and polling recovery surfaces inspected for this decision.
